title: Loud and soft, a story
summary: Mark the one loudest bar and the quietest part, then play the piece as a story that walks between them.
materials: the piece from your teacher, with a pencil

figure.alt: A row of eight boxes for the piece's bars. The sixth is shaded, standing for the one loudest bar marked in pencil; the quietest part, mentioned in the text too, is somewhere among the unshaded bars.

steps.title: Loud and soft, a story
steps.body:
The notes are right. Now make them mean something. Every piece has a shape: a quiet part, a part that grows, one moment that is the loudest, and a way home. Playing every bar at the same loudness is like reading a story in one flat voice.

1. Decide where the loudest bar is. There is only one. Mark it.
2. Decide where the quietest part is. Mark that too.
3. Play the piece as a story that walks from quiet to loud and back. Same notes, different weight in the fingers.
4. Record it and listen: can you hear the story without seeing the page?

Loud is not hitting harder. It is more arm weight into the key, and it comes with a slightly wider, calmer feel. Soft is less weight, not less confidence.

figure.alt: A row of eight boxes for the piece's bars, the sixth shaded as the loudest bar marked this week, part of playing the piece as a story from quiet to loud and home again.

steps.title: Four sittings
steps.body: Fifteen minutes each. Tick a sitting when it is done. Days do not matter; sittings do.
checklist: Sitting 1: mark the loudest bar and the quietest part on the page
Sitting 2: play the piece as a story from quiet to loud and home again
Sitting 3: record it, listen, and ask whether the story can be heard
Sitting 4: the whole piece once through with the story, then once as if recording
An old piece played with a story it never had before

steps.title: Record this week's version
steps.prompt: Say the name of the piece, then play it once through, hands in the frame. Slips stay in.
